cards.headline: A piano played by no one: the Disklavier behind the track
cards.snippet: "Avril 14th" is a piano instrumental by Richard D. James, who records as Aphex Twin. It appeared on his 2001 album Drukqs, which is otherwise mostly electronic. He recorded it on a Disklavier, a piano whose mechanism reads MIDI data and plays the keys with no one at the keyboard. You can hear the mechanism clicking in the recording. Fact writer Scott Wilson said the result sounds human, but not quite.
cards.context: From Drukqs (2001), Aphex Twin's mostly electronic double album.

cards.headline: A banned SNL short and a re-recorded Four Lions version
cards.snippet: In 2007, "Avril 14th" was sampled in a song for the Saturday Night Live digital short "Iran So Far". NBC hadn't obtained the rights to the track, so the short was taken off YouTube. It was reuploaded to SNL's official channel on August 14, 2013. Separately, for the 2010 film Four Lions, Aphex Twin (Richard D. James) re-recorded the piece with a minor edit.
cards.context: The song also appeared in Marie Antoinette and the international trailer for Her.
